arguments.query: Northstar approval Deal Desk payment schedule

executive_summary.text: OPP-1001, the Northstar Foods Cooperative Global Access Renewal, is at stage 6.0 Order Review in Commit with 78% probability. It has an ACV of 4217500 and a TCV of 12652500 on a 36-month term, and the close date is 2026-05-17.

The buyer calls this a "documentation-heavy renewal with a few governance dependencies". The CISO says she can support signature in the May window if the single final packet lands by the proposed date, framed as a renewal rather than an expansion.

Three dependencies remain: a written payment schedule for finance, an accurate data retention policy citation, and narrower liability wording in writing. Legal is "not blocking, but it is still open".

Timing is the main risk. Iris Calder is out of office 05-04 to 05-08, and her deputy cannot sign. If finance does not approve the payment schedule before 05-04, signature slips toward the 05-17 close.

Both pricing notes show an 8% renewal uplift. PN-4002 records a 0% requested discount and no new concession in final review, but PN-4001 records a 4% requested discount, so the current figure needs to be confirmed.

Site sequencing is unresolved. The March plan was pilot sites first, but a 2026-05-02 update says Pavel Stone now wants the two legacy-appliance sites first. It is unclear whether Marco Devlin agrees.

negotiation_state.stage_assessment: Late-stage order review. Business alignment is in place and the deal is now gated on documents rather than price. The remaining gates are the written payment schedule, the data retention citation, the liability redline and the consolidated packet. Timing is tight because procurement is away 05-04 to 05-08, and a new sequencing conflict has come up.
negotiation_state.customer_position: Northstar is renewing and not shopping the platform. It wants one clean order form, an uplift explanation that keeps facts separate from the recommendation, and payment milestones tied to readiness, not outcomes. It also wants success metrics with baselines (including policy drift), named owner groups and an escalation path, legacy-site review dates, and no expansion framing.
negotiation_state.vendor_position: Proposed ACV is 4217500 on an 8% uplift, and the final review recorded no new concession. The vendor committed to two payment options, narrower liability wording tied to documented service commitments, and a policy citation with an attached excerpt. It also committed to positioning the deal as a renewal with operational assurance.
open_items: Written payment schedule (standard annual vs two-milestone) for finance review before 05-04
Internal check on whether the milestone option changes total contract value or the approval path
Data retention citation with policy name, version date and excerpt
Written liability redline tied to documented service commitments
Pilot-first vs legacy-first sequencing, and Marco Devlin's view
Named owner groups for two regions and baseline exception counts
Dashboard mock and support bridge schedule
Signer arrangement if signature falls during 05-04 to 05-08
Current requested discount: PN-4001 says 4%, PN-4002 says 0%

next_actions.action: Send Northstar one consolidated final packet containing: the executive summary; success metrics with baseline and target (exception reduction, closure time, policy drift); a named owner-group matrix with escalation path; legacy-site review dates; a dashboard mock; and the support bridge schedule. Frame it as a renewal, with no expansion language.
next_actions.rationale: The CISO ties May signature support to this packet, and procurement wants one packet and no early signature ask. The infrastructure lead needs real owner groups and a support bridge schedule. Payment, legal and pricing parts are handled in separate internal actions and join the packet only after the required reviews.

next_actions.action: Internal: finalize two payment options: standard annual billing, and a two-milestone schedule tied to the first-wave readiness checklist and support bridge schedule. Confirm internally whether the milestone option changes total contract value or the approval path. Mark every item that needs vendor-side approval, and do not describe the schedule as approved.
next_actions.rationale: Finance must approve the schedule before 05-04 or signature slips. The AE said the milestone option "should not change total contract value" but still has to confirm. No discount is proposed here. If the confirmation shows a concession or a change in cost, it must go to Deal Desk under policy before anything is shared.

next_actions.action: Internal: reconcile PN-4001 (4% requested discount) with PN-4002 (0%). Then confirm the order form shows the 8% uplift, proposed ACV 4217500 and a 36-month term.
next_actions.rationale: The two notes disagree on the requested discount, so the right figure is disputed and not resolved here. At 0%, or even 4%, the discount is below the 10% Deal Desk threshold. An 8% uplift is above the 0% floor. So these figures would not trigger Deal Desk or sales leader approval. Any change beyond those thresholds would need those approvals.

next_actions.action: Internal: prepare the data retention citation, including the policy name, version date and attached excerpt. Route it to vendor legal for review before it goes into the packet.
next_actions.rationale: Customer legal is not blocking but will reopen redlines if the citation is wrong. The action carries the data_retention and legal_terms tags, so it needs legal approval under policy before it is shared externally.

next_actions.action: Internal: draft the written liability redline, narrowing the obligation to documented service commitments rather than indirect business interruption. Avoid any "guarantee" language and any side-email assurances.
next_actions.rationale: Customer legal asked for this in writing. The action carries the legal_terms tag, so it needs legal approval. Legal must also decide whether the change counts as a liability cap change, which under policy needs legal approval before customer-facing language is produced.

proposed_values.liability_cap_change: Narrow liability wording to tie obligations to documented service commitments rather than indirect business interruption; legal to determine whether this constitutes a cap change.

next_actions.action: Internal: draft the uplift explanation memo. Put commercial facts (term, covered products, billing options, migration deliverables) in a table and keep the recommendation separate. Tie the uplift to evidence that exception risk goes down.
next_actions.rationale: Procurement needs to document why the renewal is not flat. The CISO said she can defend the uplift if given evidence that the renewal reduces exception risk. The memo contains pricing content, so it stays internal until it has been reviewed.

next_actions.action: Hold a short joint session with Marco Devlin and Pavel Stone to confirm the first-wave site list and sequencing, the named owner groups for both regions, and the baseline exception counts.
next_actions.rationale: Sources disagree on whether pilot sites or legacy sites go first, and Marco Devlin's view is unknown. The success metrics and owner matrix depend on this, so the action rests on the disputed point. The customer said baselines are needed so the metrics are not hand-wavy.

next_actions.action: Before 4 May, confirm with Iris Calder the finance review timeline for the signature package, and who at Northstar can sign if signature falls between 4 and 8 May.
next_actions.rationale: Iris's deputy can receive the package but cannot sign. Finance review must finish before her absence or signature drifts toward the 05-17 close.

next_actions.action: Internal: send the sequencing conflict and the pricing-note discount discrepancy to a human reviewer before the final packet is released.
next_actions.rationale: Policy requires conflicting evidence to go to a human reviewer. Both conflicts affect packet content: the owner matrix, the success metrics and the order form figures.
